cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “A side-space cushion leaves room to”.
cards.back: A side-space cushion leaves room to move right or left if needed.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Avoid staying alongside another vehicle because its blind spot”.
cards.back: Avoid staying alongside another vehicle because its blind spot and a reduced escape space can expose you to a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Keep away from the centerline when”.
cards.back: Keep away from the centerline when possible to leave room from oncoming traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Help entering vehicles by changing lanes or”.
cards.back: Help entering vehicles by changing lanes or adjusting speed when making room is possible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Give pedestrians and bicyclists extra space, especially children, and”.
cards.back: Give pedestrians and bicyclists extra space, especially children, and wait to pass in an adjacent lane rather than remain alongside.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “When a large vehicle passes, move toward the outside”.
cards.back: When a large vehicle passes, move toward the outside part of your lane to increase side clearance from it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “On multilane roads, move ahead or fall back rather”.
cards.back: On multilane roads, move ahead or fall back rather than remain beside a vehicle that may crowd your lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Leave extra space beside parked cars”.
cards.back: Leave extra space beside parked cars because a person or vehicle may emerge.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “When positioned between hazards, split the available space”.
cards.back: When positioned between hazards, split the available space but give more room to the more dangerous side.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “When approaching a bicycle and oncoming traffic together, slowing”.
cards.back: When approaching a bicycle and oncoming traffic together, slowing until the oncoming vehicle passes can let you pass the bicycle with more room.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “A steady speed and early slowdown or turn”.
cards.back: A steady speed and early slowdown or turn signals help a following driver maintain a safe gap.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Pick up or drop off passengers in”.
cards.back: Pick up or drop off passengers in a safe place outside traffic when possible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Before parallel parking with approaching traffic behind, signal beside”.
cards.back: Before parallel parking with approaching traffic behind, signal beside the space and allow following vehicles to pass first.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Use the rightmost lane when slower than other traffic”.
cards.back: Use the rightmost lane when slower than other traffic on a multilane road and pull aside safely if you are holding vehicles up.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “If tailgated and a right lane exists, move right;”.
cards.back: If tailgated and a right lane exists, move right; otherwise wait for a clear, legal passing opportunity before reducing speed gradually.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Never brake abruptly to discourage a”.
cards.back: Never brake abruptly to discourage a tailgater because doing so increases rear-impact risk.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about side and rear space, beginning with “Allow large trucks and buses extra room because”.
cards.back: Allow large trucks and buses extra room because they cannot stop as quickly as a car.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Pass only where signs or markings allow it and”.
cards.back: Pass only where signs or markings allow it and enough safe space exists, generally taking one vehicle at a time on the left.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Complete a pass promptly and return safely”.
cards.back: Complete a pass promptly and return safely rather than lingering in the passing lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “The handbook’s fifty-five-mile-per-hour example allows about ten seconds for”.
cards.back: The handbook’s fifty-five-mile-per-hour example allows about ten seconds for passing and requires a corresponding oncoming gap and sight distance.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “At fifty-five miles per hour, the handbook says each”.
cards.back: At fifty-five miles per hour, the handbook says each opposing vehicle travels over eight hundred feet in ten seconds, requiring over one thousand six hundred feet, about one-third mile, of combined clear distance.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Faraway vehicles may appear still or slower than they”.
cards.back: Faraway vehicles may appear still or slower than they are, so wait to pass when the available gap is uncertain.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “The handbook advises at least one-third mile, about ten”.
cards.back: The handbook advises at least one-third mile, about ten seconds, of visibility and no passing within that distance of a hill or curve hiding opposing traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Do not pass where vehicles may enter or”.
cards.back: Do not pass where vehicles may enter or cross, including intersections, rail crossings and shopping-center entrances.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “A vehicle being passed can block the view of”.
cards.back: A vehicle being passed can block the view of road users or trains, and a turning driver may not expect a vehicle in the opposing lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “The handbook compares a typical fifteen-foot car with a”.
cards.back: The handbook compares a typical fifteen-foot car with a multi-trailer truck at least seventy-five feet long to explain why truck passing takes more time and clear road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Before passing, look for pedestrians or cyclists, narrow lanes,”.
cards.back: Before passing, look for pedestrians or cyclists, narrow lanes, ice, potholes or objects that could push another vehicle into the passing lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Do not pass without room to return to the”.
cards.back: Do not pass without room to return to the normal lane, and never assume other drivers will create that room.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Do not pass with”.
cards.back: Do not pass with a rail grade crossing ahead.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about passing space, beginning with “Before returning after a pass, leave enough separation and”.
cards.back: Before returning after a pass, leave enough separation and ensure both headlights of the passed vehicle appear in the rearview mirror.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “Give extra space to people who may not see”.
cards.back: Give extra space to people who may not see you, including drivers with blocked views, reversing vehicles, obscured windows and pedestrians whose vision is obstructed or who use a white cane or guide dog.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “Allow extra room or caution around potentially distracted”.
cards.back: Allow extra room or caution around potentially distracted delivery workers, construction workers, children and inattentive drivers.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “Potentially confused road users include unfamiliar visitors, drivers searching”.
cards.back: Potentially confused road users include unfamiliar visitors, drivers searching for signs or addresses, unexplained slow drivers and pedestrians affected by alcohol.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “Large trucks and buses need extra maneuvering room, including”.
cards.back: Large trucks and buses need extra maneuvering room, including in roundabouts, and extra-wide loads need as much clearance as possible.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “If another driver misjudges a pass or needs a”.
cards.back: If another driver misjudges a pass or needs a sudden lane change, slow enough to let the driver return or merge safely rather than worsen the error.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “Separate hazards when possible by adjusting timing”.
cards.back: Separate hazards when possible by adjusting timing so they are passed one at a time.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about separating hazards, beginning with “When simultaneous hazards cannot be separated, give the larger”.
cards.back: When simultaneous hazards cannot be separated, give the larger space cushion to the greater danger, such as an unpredictable child on a bicycle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Headlights help others see the vehicle whenever”.
cards.back: Headlights help others see the vehicle whenever visibility is poor, including rain, snow and fog.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “The handbook recommends turning on headlights when the”.
cards.back: The handbook recommends turning on headlights when the wipers are needed and when daylight begins fading.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Use headlights rather than parking lamps when driving”.
cards.back: Use headlights rather than parking lamps when driving requires lights, because parking lamps serve parked vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Use headlights when driving away from a low rising”.
cards.back: Use headlights when driving away from a low rising or setting sun so oncoming drivers facing glare can see the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “High beams improve distant night visibility when there is”.
cards.back: High beams improve distant night visibility when there is no oncoming vehicle; the handbook describes the visible distance as twice that of low beams.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Dim high beams within five”.
cards.back: Dim high beams within five hundred feet of an approaching vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Use low beams when following another vehicle at less”.
cards.back: Use low beams when following another vehicle at less than five hundred feet or driving in heavy traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Use low beams in fog, snow or heavy rain”.
cards.back: Use low beams in fog, snow or heavy rain because reflected high-beam light causes glare; use fitted fog lamps in those conditions too.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Never drive with only”.
cards.back: Never drive with only the parking lamps illuminated.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “If an oncoming driver does not dim, briefly flash”.
cards.back: If an oncoming driver does not dim, briefly flash the high beams; if glare continues, look toward the right road edge until that vehicle passes.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Daytime running lamps improve daytime visibility but do not”.
cards.back: Daytime running lamps improve daytime visibility but do not replace headlights at night or in fog, rain or snow.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about headlights and visibility, beginning with “Without daytime running lamps, manually using headlights provides similar”.
cards.back: Without daytime running lamps, manually using headlights provides similar daytime visibility, but remember to turn them off after shutting down the engine.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “Use the horn to communicate a crash risk,”.
cards.back: Use the horn to communicate a crash risk, with a light tap when no immediate danger exists.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “A light horn tap can warn a pedestrian or”.
cards.back: A light horn tap can warn a pedestrian or cyclist moving toward the lane, but at an intersection crossing yield instead of sounding the horn at them.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “A light tap may warn a passed driver turning”.
cards.back: A light tap may warn a passed driver turning toward your lane or a driver who is inattentive or cannot see you.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “A light horn warning may be useful where a”.
cards.back: A light horn warning may be useful where a steep hill, sharp curve or narrow alley exit blocks the view ahead.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “Use a sharp horn blast when another vehicle may”.
cards.back: Use a sharp horn blast when another vehicle may hit you or when your own uncontrolled vehicle is moving toward someone.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “Do not use the horn to hurry a”.
cards.back: Do not use the horn to hurry a driver, criticize an error or greet a friend.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about horn use, beginning with “Do not sound the horn around blind pedestrians,”.
cards.back: Do not sound the horn around blind pedestrians, animal-drawn vehicles or animals being herded on the road.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about breakdown warnings, beginning with “If a vehicle breaks down, warn others with flares”.
cards.back: If a vehicle breaks down, warn others with flares or triangles behind it and contact authorities by phone if one is available.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about breakdown warnings, beginning with “For vehicle trouble, move off the road and away”.
cards.back: For vehicle trouble, move off the road and away from traffic when possible and activate the four-way emergency flashers.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about breakdown warnings, beginning with “If the disabled vehicle cannot get fully off the”.
cards.back: If the disabled vehicle cannot get fully off the road, stop where it is visible rather than just past a hill or around a curve.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about breakdown warnings, beginning with “Stand safely away from the roadway and use available”.
cards.back: Stand safely away from the roadway and use available warning devices; never change a tire from within a traffic lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about breakdown warnings, beginning with “A raised hood or white cloth tied to the”.
cards.back: A raised hood or white cloth tied to the antenna, side mirror or door handle can signal a vehicle emergency.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about no zones, beginning with “Avoid another vehicle’s side-and-rear blind area by moving ahead”.
cards.back: Avoid another vehicle’s side-and-rear blind area by moving ahead or dropping back, and pass through that blind area promptly.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about no zones, beginning with “Do not remain directly beside or”.
cards.back: Do not remain directly beside or immediately behind a large truck or bus.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about no zones, beginning with “The handbook’s truck No Zone includes blind areas up”.
cards.back: The handbook’s truck No Zone includes blind areas up to twenty feet in front of the cab, beside it and up to two hundred feet behind.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about no zones, beginning with “As a rule of thumb, if the truck or”.
cards.back: As a rule of thumb, if the truck or bus driver is not visible in the side mirror, assume your vehicle is not visible to that driver.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “Warn other drivers before changing direction or”.
cards.back: Warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to react.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “Signal before lane changes, turns, merging, parking and both”.
cards.back: Signal before lane changes, turns, merging, parking and both the start and finish of a pass, even when nobody else is apparent.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “The handbook gives a turn-signal distance of one hundred”.
cards.back: The handbook gives a turn-signal distance of one hundred feet but warns against signaling before an intervening street, driveway or entrance where another driver could misunderstand.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “If another vehicle may enter between you and the”.
cards.back: If another vehicle may enter between you and the intended turn, pass that vehicle’s entry point before signaling the turn.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “After a turn or lane change,”.
cards.back: After a turn or lane change, confirm that the turn signal has stopped.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “Slow as early as safely possible and tap the”.
cards.back: Slow as early as safely possible and tap the brake pedal three or four times before an unexpected slowdown or stop to warn following traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “Give advance slowdown warning for a turn without a”.
cards.back: Give advance slowdown warning for a turn without a separate turn lane, parking or turning just before an intersection, or a hidden road obstruction or traffic queue.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “Hand signals can supplement turn lamps in bright sun”.
cards.back: Hand signals can supplement turn lamps in bright sun or serve an antique vehicle built before July one, nineteen fifty-eight that may lack those lamps.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “For a left hand-and-arm turn”.
cards.back: For a left hand-and-arm turn signal, extend the hand straight outward.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “For a right hand-and-arm turn”.
cards.back: For a right hand-and-arm turn signal, point the hand upward.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about movement signals, beginning with “For a stop or slowdown”.
cards.back: For a stop or slowdown hand signal, point the hand downward.
